claims.statement: The original E-006 SQLite reference suite passed on commit 550e460ba31f326a1eb6cdcbc0556567809cbe53.
Independent processes opening the same SQLite file cannot both acquire the same unexpired task lease.
claims.required_run: e006-recovery workflow on exact PR head

claims.statement: An abrupt process exit with an open SQLite transaction leaves no partial local effect or completion state after reopen.
claims.required_run: e006-recovery workflow on exact PR head

claims.statement: A transactional outbox preserves publication intent, but a relay crash after broker acknowledgement and before marking the outbox row can produce duplicate delivery; a transactional consumer inbox can suppress duplicate local effects.
claims.boundary: The harness uses independent SQLite files and a deterministic fake broker. It does not prove a real broker, payment provider, email service, or arbitrary HTTP receiver honors idempotency.

claims.statement: Versioned checksummed migrations, bounded terminal-record retention, WAL checkpointing, VACUUM and integrity checks behave as asserted by the executable model.
claims.required_run: e006-recovery workflow on exact PR head

claims.statement: No production persistence substrate is selected by this experiment.
claims.rationale: SQLite reference correctness is not a comparative workload benchmark or evidence of multi-node coordination. PostgreSQL and MySQL remain candidates pending identical conformance, failure-injection, workload, recovery and operational-cost measurements.

limitations: SQLite tests exercise one shared local filesystem and do not establish distributed locks, multi-host fencing, consensus, or HA.
A lease token fences database writes only when every state transition checks it; it cannot stop a stale process from completing an external request.
External publication is at-least-once. Exactly-once external effects require a downstream idempotency contract, or explicit reconciliation/compensation when that contract is absent.
Retention deletion is irreversible for the deleted rows; production policy must define replay windows, legal holds, audit requirements and archival before enabling cleanup.
VACUUM requires operational headroom and an exclusive maintenance window appropriate to the selected SQLite mode; this prototype does not establish a production compaction schedule.
